newsitem.title: GERMANY: Nervous German shares look to U.S. for signals.
newsitem.headline: Nervous German shares look to U.S. for signals.

text.p: A nervous German share market was sharply lower on Monday as traders predicted the 30-share DAX index would remain under pressure until Wall Street opens.

At 0710 GMT, the IBIS DAX index, which reflects all-day computer trade, was down 98.24 points at 3,979.35 points, or a loss of 2.4 percent, as the index tumbled through 4,000 points with little resistance.
The IBIS DAX was more than four percent below the bourse DAX close on Friday at 4,152.86 points.
Dealers were debating whether the DAX would begin to pare some of its heavy losses or keep falling to fresh losses.
They noted that the DAX index on Friday fell about 1.9 percent in bourse dealings and posted heavy losses in post-bourse computer dealings later in the day.
In addition, they said Germany's low interest rates and favourable environment for higher corporate earnings may prompt the German market to outperform the U.S. share market.
Some traders also said the bourse opening will be important to gauge the reaction of private investors to the market's sharp decline, which has been prompted by a weak dollar.
"It looks like there is a chance we could stabilise between 3,900 and 4,000 points," said one Frankfurt trader.
"But it will also be critical to see if private investors are overly nervous and add to the selling pressure in the bourse session," he said.
Trading volumes were heavy as top DAX components, including many export-senstive shares that posted hefty gains as the dollar surged toward 1.90 marks, were hit for losses.

Among those lower were luxury carmaker Porsche AG, which fell 159 marks to 2,331 marks, and Volkswagen AG, which fell 28.50 marks to 1,224.50 marks ahead of its half-year results due out later on Monday.
Banking shares, propped up recently by speculation for a wave of mergers and takeovers, posted among the worst losses.
Commerzbank AG, considered a top takeover candidate, was down 2.70 marks at 62.35 marks and Deutsche Bank AG was down 3.20 marks at 110.55 marks.
BHF Bank, considered to be a takeover target, was among the top percentage loss leaders, as was Bankgesellschaft Berlin.
BHF fell 4.14 marks to 51.01 marks, while Bankgesellschaft Berlin slumped 3.30 marks to 44 marks.
